Checking Your Polarity.

So I want you to just take your palm, put that a little bit over there. Now, you should sway naturally, and in an organized state, your body should gently rock forward. Like I said, it's not going to be dramatic. It's just going to be, you're going to feel a little pull or sensation in the chest. Now, we're going to test again. We're going to turn the palm the other way over the crown. You're going to stay in the same relaxed position. Your body should naturally rock backwards. If your body rocked backward when the palm was facing down, or if you rocked forward when the palm was facing up, that means that your polarity is reversed or disorganized. And if you didn't go anywhere, it's still disorganized if it's neutral.

So checking the polarity, we can reset the polarity with Cook's crossover technique. You know the saying 'out of sorts' or 'feeling out of whack'? Put your hands together, we're going to interlace, and you're going to bring the palms towards the chest. For you yogis, it's just like the eagle pose. So you're crossing the hands at the wrist so that the top hand is opposite the top leg. Turn the wrists until the palms face each other and interlace your fingers. Keeping this grasp, fold arms inward, bringing the hands to the chest. And then I want you to, if you can, press the tip of your tongue to the palate just behind the two front teeth and hold this position for several minutes. Sometimes I just have Alexa set a timer for about three minutes. And so we wait. And while you're waiting, you should start to feel the body relax, like tension melting away, like a deep wave of relaxation. After about three minutes, you can uncross the ankles, take the hands away. We're going to take the fingertips now and place them together like in a steeple position. Sometimes, I mean, you can even do it before bed or when you wake up and you're feeling off. I know somebody who does it in the dentist chair. And if so, then you're going to turn the palm, we're going to test the second way, and you should go backwards. If you find that you're still moving in the opposite directions, then you can reset, but this time you'll do it with the opposite leg. So I'll cross my left over my right, take my hands out, I'll put my right this time over the left wrist, we're going to clap the hands together, interlace the fingers, and bring the palms in. Again, you can set it for about three minutes, even a minute, and then we'll reset again, both feet on the floor, take the fingertips, put them together in about a steeple position, take the thumb, put it towards your third eye, hold again for a minute. And then we'll retest and see. Taking the palm, if you want, you guys, a great idea too is to even like sensitize the hands again like we did in the first episode. Clap. Really get, start to feel the resistance, the sensation. Then take the palm over the crown. Breathe so, and you should start to be pulled forward a little bit. When I turn the palm over, should be feeling, I'm like really feeling it now that we've reset it, like that little pull backwards. And that's Cook's crossover.

videoAnalyses.title: The Nth Degree Healing - 7 Chakras UPDATED
videoAnalyses.summary: This video provides a concise overview of the seven main chakras in the human body. It explains their locations, functions, physical associations, and the symptoms that manifest when they are imbalanced.
videoAnalyses.fullTranscript:
There are seven main chakras in the body. When we understand where they are and each function, then we can understand the emotional responses or the physical manifestations when they're blocked. So let's go through that right now.

The root chakra, located at the base of the spine. Its main function are your primal needs: safety, security, and your shelter. The physical associations with the root chakra are your legs, feet, bones, and your large intestine. When imbalanced, it can manifest as lower back pain, sciatica, varicose veins, or constipation. And your root chakra is associated with the color red.

Your sacral chakra, the second chakra, is located between the pubic bone and the navel. Its function is for creativity, pleasure, sexuality. It's physically associated with your reproductive organs, your bladder, your lower back. So when imbalanced, it may result in urinary tract infections, lower back pain, or fertility issues.

The third chakra is your solar plexus chakra. Its location is in your upper abdomen, between the navel and the base of your breastplate. Its main function is your personal power, self-esteem, self-worth, and your decision-making. Its physical associations are the digestive system, your pancreas, and adrenal glands. When imbalanced, it can lead to digestive issues, diabetes, or adrenal fatigue. Your solar plexus chakra is associated with the color yellow, just like the sun.

The heart chakra. It's located at the center of your chest. Its main function is love, compassion, empathy. Its physical associations are the heart, the lungs, the chest, the arms, and the hands. When imbalanced, it might manifest as heart problems, asthma, or upper back pain. Your heart chakra is the bridge between the lower body and the upper body. And this heart chakra is associated with the color green.

Your throat chakra, located in your throat area. Its main function is communication and self-expression. The physical associations with the throat chakra are throat, thyroid, mouth, neck. And when imbalanced, it can result in thyroid problems, sore throats, or neck pain. Your throat chakra is associated with the color blue.

Your third eye chakra. It's located in the middle of your forehead, right above the eyebrows. Its main function is your wisdom, your intuition, and insight. The physical associations with the third eye chakra are your brain, eyes, sinuses, pituitary gland. And when imbalanced, it may lead to headaches, vision problems, or hormonal imbalances. The third eye chakra is associated with the color indigo.

The crown chakra is located at the top of your head. Its function is your spiritual connection and enlightenment. The physical associations are the central nervous system and the cerebral cortex. When imbalanced, it can manifest as depression, chronic fatigue, or sensitivity to light and sound. And your crown chakra is associated with the color purple.

lessons.title: Map all seven chakras to your body so you can recognize imbalance by its symptoms
lessons.summary: Learners systematically locate each of the seven chakras from root to crown, identify the function, color, physical organ associations, and imbalance symptoms for each, and leave with a personal body map they can use to trace physical or emotional discomfort back to a specific energy center.

sessions.title: The Seven Chakras: Location, Function, and Imbalance Symptoms from Root to Crown
sessions.summary: A focused tour of all seven main chakras — root, sacral, solar plexus, heart, throat, third eye, and crown — covering where each lives in the body, what it governs emotionally and physically, and how to recognize it when it is out of balance.

steps.title: Build your personal seven-chakra symptom map and flag your highest-priority energy center
Reflect on the connection between a current physical symptom and its chakra

clips.chapterTitle: Why Chakras Matter and a Complete Tour of the Root, Sacral, Solar Plexus, and Heart Chakras
